node.name: Yale INSPIRE: Ananth Sriskandarajah, Founder and CEO of Greenweaver AI
node.descriptionText:
Yale INSPIRE is a speaker series that brings visionary founders, innovators, and changemakers to campus for candid conversations about the moments that shaped their journeys. Go beyond the headlines to hear about the lessons, setbacks, breakthroughs, and bold decisions behind building what’s next.

​In partnership with the Yale AI Association, join us for a fireside chat with Ananth Sriskandarajah, Founder and CEO of Greenweaver AI, exploring what it takes to build at the intersection of AI, climate, and infrastructure.

​Greenweaver AI is building sovereign, low-carbon AI infrastructure through modular micro data centers that combine high-performance computing with heat reuse. Ananth’s work focuses on the intersection of AI, climate, infrastructure, and institutional capital.

​Previously, Ananth served as Managing Director and Head of Ventures at Round Hill Capital, where he launched and led its venture strategy, invested across Europe, and served on the Investment Committee and Executive Committee. Earlier in his career, he held leadership roles at HelloFresh, Bloomsbury AI, and The Collective, and worked across strategy and investment at Capital & Counties PLC. He also served as an Entrepreneur in Residence at the European Commission supporting StartupEurope.

​Ananth is also the Founder of Ground Floor Ventures, an angel syndicate backing ambitious early-stage founders. He has been recognized in WIRED 100 and Forbes 30 Under 30.

​Whether you’re building your first startup, curious about the future of AI, or interested in how technology, climate, and capital intersect, come hear directly from a leader working across these rapidly evolving fields.

A networking reception and light bites to follow!

node.name: Science Policy and Congress: Workshop and Info Session
node.descriptionText:
After the 2026 Midterm elections, are you interested in: What role does Congress play in science policy? Does advocacy really make a difference? How do I apply to Yale's Science Policy Hill Day program?

In this second fall workshop, we'll build on the first workshop on science policy communication to dive deeper into Congress' role in science policy and how to influence science policy. This session is also HIGHLY recommended if you plan on applying to the Hill Day program, as we'll share more details on this year's application process and what group work during the spring looks like.

Yale Science Policy Hill Day is a university-wide initiative that invites students from all disciplines to explore the intersection of science and policy. This fall, we are hosting two open workshops designed to give students hands-on experience with science advocacy. Afterward, applications will open for our spring cohort, where selected students will receive additional training to prepare for meetings with policymakers in Washington, DC during our culminating Hill Day. Learn more at https://sciencepolicy.yale.edu/.

node.name: Advanced Search Techniques
node.descriptionText: Learn skills to research like a librarian, including how to use "advanced search" techniques to find books and articles in Quicksearch.
node.descriptionHtml:
Learn skills to research like a librarian, including how to use "advanced search" techniques to find books and articles in Quicksearch. Join us for 30-minutes and get a step ahead for coursework and research projects!

Attendees will learn how to:

  • navigate to distinct resource types in Quicksearch (books, articles, etc.)

  • use filters (subject, author, discipline) to find more relevant results

  • identify Advanced Search features

  • broaden and narrow search results using operators AND, OR, and NOT

Audience: Undergraduate students. Graduate students are also welcome.

Students interested in this workshop might also be interested in “First Steps with Zotero” and "Demystifying the Literature Review." For individual support, reach out to your Personal Librarian or Subject Specialist Librarian.

Any student who attends at least 3 library workshops this semester will be eligible to receive a Yale Library tote bag! Learn more about the Workshop Incentive Program.

node.name: 2026 Midterm Elections: What Have We Learned & What Comes Next
node.descriptionText:
What messages were voters trying to send at the federal and state levels? What can Americans expect for governance over the next two years?

Join political scientists Alan Gerber (moderator) and panelists Christina Kinane, Josh Kalla, and pollster Zachary Donnini (Yale ’25, VoteHub) for a conversation about the 2026 midterm election results. We will provide analysis of election data, discuss the composition of the 120th Congress, preview agenda items for lawmakers, and talk about the governance implications for how the new Congress might interact with the administration. We will also take time to answer audience questions.

node.name: Volunteer with Sunrise Cafe!
node.descriptionText:
Start your morning off on a great note! Join Dwight Hall Monday and Wednesday mornings to volunteer at Sunrise Cafe. Sunrise Cafe is an early morning soup kitchen that serves New Haven's homeless and food-insecure every weekday from 6:30 A.M. to 8:30 A.M. The service site is located at 57 Olive St., just a 15 minute walk from Phelps Gate. Volunteers will meet in front of Phelps Gate at 6:00am, walk together to Sunrise Cafe, and will return to campus by 9:00am.

To sign up, please request to join DWIGHT HALL VOLUNTEER CORPS, and we will approve your request as soon as possible.

Sunrise Cafe has been serving breakfast without charge to New Haven's homeless and hungry since 2015. Each weekday morning, the Cafe welcomes guests to the undercroft of St. Paul and St. James, near Wooster Square and three blocks south of the New Haven Green with white tablecloths, flowers and a rotating menu of fresh, warm, nutritious home-cooked food. Your generosity opens our doors.

Cheerful volunteers take each order individually, deliver the breakfast to our guest and help our paid chefs in the kitchen. Staff and volunteers ensure every guest is warmly welcomed.

Sunrise Cafe is uniquely welcoming and secure, based on trust and mutual respect, and the rapport built between the volunteer servers and our guests. With a warm welcome and just two rules – no drugs on the premises and no arguments – Sunrise has become a community center for the homeless, a place to come every weekday morning and gather with friends.

Hungry friends come for the home-cooked, nourishing breakfast and stay for simple medical services offered by the Cornell Scott Health Center and access to support from social services to find housing.

Sunrise provides a unique opportunity to bridge New Haven's inequalities that separate us from one another. Volunteers come once and become regulars. Guests and volunteers become friends and greet one another on the street.

If you have any questions, email maryann.dang@yale.edu

node.name: Barbara J Turpin - Implications of the use of PFAS
node.descriptionText:
Department of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Gillings School of Global Public Health
University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used for their heat-, stain-, and water-resistant properties, but they are persistent, bioaccumulative, and associated with adverse health effects. While most PFAS research has focused on water, PFAS are also transported via air, where measurements remain scarce. This talk will describe our efforts to characterize airborne PFAS indoors and near manufacturing facilities, where they are most likely to influence human exposure. Using integrated sampling
with LC/MS and GC/MS, we found elevated fluorotelomer alcohols and perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids downwind of a facility and in homes. Inhalation of neutral PFAS was the largest non-dietary contributor to residential exposure. Real-time chemical ionization mass spectrometry also shows promise for studying PFAS dynamics and occupational exposure.
